# EtherNet/IP Receiver

This receiver polls tags from EtherNet/IP (CIP) devices, such as PLCs, and reports device reachability and tag values as metrics.

The receiver connects to a single EtherNet/IP device, reads a configured list
of tags by symbolic name on every collection interval, and emits each value as
a gauge. It also emits a reachability gauge, so a device that stops responding
is visible even when no tag values arrive. The receiver is read-only: it never
writes tags or changes device state.

## Supported devices

Tags are addressed by symbolic name using the Logix Symbol Object, via the
[`gologix`](https://github.com/danomagnum/gologix) client library. This means:

- **Supported:** Rockwell Automation ControlLogix, CompactLogix and Micro820 controllers.
- **Not supported:** PCCC-based controllers (PLC-5, SLC 500, MicroLogix), and
  non-Rockwell EtherNet/IP devices that don't implement symbolic tag access.
  Generic CIP object (Class/Instance/Attribute) access is on the
  [roadmap](./DESIGN.md#roadmap).
- **Not supported:** CIP Security (TLS/DTLS). Connections are unencrypted and
  unauthenticated, as is typical for EtherNet/IP.

### Supported tag data types

Each tag value is converted to a `float64`. The following Logix data types can
be read today:

| Logix type | Reported as |
|---|---|
| `LREAL` | the value |
| `DINT` | the value |
| `BOOL` | `1` (true) or `0` (false) |

Other types, including `REAL`, `SINT`, `INT`, `LINT`, the unsigned integer
types, `STRING`, arrays and UDTs, are **not read** at this stage: the tag is
logged as unreadable and skipped on each scrape.

## Prerequisites

- The collector must be able to reach the device on TCP port `44818` (or the
  port you configure).
- Each receiver instance holds one CIP connection open to the device. Controllers
  support a limited number of concurrent connections, so account for this when
  other HMIs, historians or engineering tools also connect to the same controller.
- Tag names must match the controller's tag names exactly, including case.

## Configuration

The following settings are required:

- `host` (no default): IP address or hostname of the device. Do not include a
  port; use `port` instead.
- `tags` (no default): List of tag names to read on every scrape. Must contain
  at least one tag.

The following settings are optional:

- `port` (default = `44818`): TCP port of the device's EtherNet/IP interface.
  Must be between `0` and `65535`; `0` uses the client library's default (`44818`).
- `device_name` (no default): A user-friendly name for the device. When set, it
  is reported as the `ethernetip.device.name` resource attribute; otherwise the
  attribute is omitted.
- `timeout` (default = `5s`): Socket timeout for each request to the device.
  Note that the collector's scraper controller also reads the `timeout` key as
  the overall scrape deadline, so an explicit value applies to both.
- `collection_interval` (default = `1m`): How often the receiver polls the
  device. This value must be a string readable by Golang's
  [time.ParseDuration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration). Valid time
  units are `ns`, `us` (or `µs`), `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`.
- `initial_delay` (default = `1s`): How long the receiver waits before the first scrape.
- `metrics` (default: all enabled): Enable or disable individual metrics. See
  [documentation.md](./documentation.md).
- `resource_attributes` (default: all enabled): Enable or disable individual
  resource attributes. See [documentation.md](./documentation.md).

Example:

```yaml
receivers:
  ethernetip:
    host: "192.168.1.10"
    device_name: "line1-plc"
    collection_interval: 10s
    tags:
      - temperature
      - pumpstatus
```

Example with one receiver per device, since each receiver instance polls a
single device:

```yaml
receivers:
  ethernetip/line1:
    host: "192.168.1.10"
    device_name: "line1-plc"
    tags: [temperature, pumpstatus]
  ethernetip/line2:
    host: "192.168.1.11"
    device_name: "line2-plc"
    tags: [temperature, pumpstatus]

service:
  pipelines:
    metrics:
      receivers: [ethernetip/line1, ethernetip/line2]
      exporters: [debug]
```

The full list of settings exposed for this receiver are documented in
[config.go](./config.go) with detailed sample configurations in
[testdata/config.yaml](./testdata/config.yaml). A complete, runnable collector
configuration is in [config.example.yaml](./config.example.yaml).

## Metrics

Details about the metrics produced by this receiver can be found in
[metadata.yaml](./metadata.yaml) with further documentation in
[documentation.md](./documentation.md).

In summary:

| Metric | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ethernetip.device.up` | Gauge (int) | `1` if the device responded on the last scrape, otherwise `0`. |
| `ethernetip.tag.value` | Gauge (double) | Current value of each configured tag, with the `ethernetip.tag.name` attribute. |

Every metric carries the `ethernetip.device.address` resource attribute, and
`ethernetip.device.name` when `device_name` is configured.

`ethernetip.tag.value` is reported with unit `1` because the receiver does not
know the engineering unit of a tag.

## Behavior

- **Startup:** If the device can't be reached when the collector starts, the
  receiver logs a warning and starts anyway. It tries to reconnect on every scrape.
- **Health check:** Each scrape first sends an EtherNet/IP `ListIdentity`
  request, rather than relying on a cached connection state. If it fails, the
  receiver tries to reconnect once.
- **Device unreachable:** `ethernetip.device.up` is reported as `0`, a warning
  is logged, and no tag values are emitted for that scrape.
- **Tag read failure:** The tag is logged at `warn` level and skipped, and the
  remaining tags are still read. Tag failures are not reported as scrape errors.
- **Load on the device:** Tags are read one request at a time. Unsupported tag
  types cost up to three requests per scrape. Keep `collection_interval`
  conservative on production controllers.

## Using this receiver in a collector

This receiver is not included in the OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib
distribution. Add it to your own distribution with the
[OpenTelemetry Collector Builder](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/custom-collector/)
(`ocb`):

```yaml
receivers:
  - gomod: github.com/otel-industrial/otel-industrial-resources/otel-industrial-collector/receiver/ethernetipreceiver v0.0.1 # use the latest released tag
```

This component is built and tested against collector v0.152.0. Use the same
`otelcol_version` in your builder manifest.

To build and run a local test collector, or try the receiver against the
included simulator without hardware, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md).
